newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power mixed in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power mixed in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic were mixed Tuesday in light, pre-holiday trading amid a rebound in the natural gas market after recent weakness tied to a forecast of mild weather .
"It's a little firmer than yesterday. The dailies were a little busy," said an East Coast broker.

Temperatures in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Inteconnect district New Year's Day were predicted to run near-normal with day readings in 30-40 degrees Fahrenheit and night readings in the teens to the 30s.
A mild weather system will likely push thermometers eight to 12 degrees above normal by Saturday.

Swing natural gas prices enjoyed a rebound today since they began plummeting last week. Daily deliveries to the Philadelphia city gate were notionally assessed in the $3.50-$3.60 per million British thermal unit range, up from Monday's $3.40-$3.50.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures rose 4.3 cents at $2.720/mmBtu.
Thursday electricity for firm, peak PJM delivery was quoted at $18.00-$19.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), a tighter range than Monday's $17.00-$19.00 for Tuesday.
Wednesday's PJM peak, firm deliveries were thinly talked in a $17.00-$18.00 range.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Thursday climbed to $15.00-$16.00, up from $14.00-$15.00 Monday.
January 1997 PJM electricity with similar delivery terms softened to $27.10-$27.40 from Monday's $27.30-$27.60.
February PJM power was valued at $28.75-$29.75, higher than $28.50-$29.00 Monday.
March PJM electricity was assessed at $24.00-$24.50, flat from Monday.
First-quarter PJM deliveries edged up to $26.60-$27.20 from Monday's $26.50-$27.00.
Most PJM deferred quotes were quiet against Monday's levels. July/August PJM climbed to $31.80-$31.25 from $31.00-$31.50 Monday.
PECO Energy Co's 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick unit 2 would hold at 88 percent of production capacity ahead of a refueling outage scheduled to begin January 31.
